title: Sri Lanka with children, without the long drives
standfirst: How we shorten the road and where the early starts are worth it.
dek: How we shorten the road and where the early starts are worth it.

author.name: The Travedise team
author.role: Travel designers in Galle and Bundeena

image.alt: A child watching the road from the jeep

text: Sri Lanka is small on the map and slow on the road. Sixty kilometres can take two hours. With children, that single fact shapes the whole trip.
So we plan family routes the other way round: fewer bases, shorter hops, and the long drives broken up with something worth stopping for.

For ten days we usually suggest three places: the Cultural Triangle, the hills or Kandy, and a stretch of coast. Staying three or four nights in each means unpacking once, learning where the pool is, and letting the children settle.
We keep most drives under three hours, and put a stop in the middle of the longer ones: a spice garden, a waterfall, a roadside king coconut.

body.text: Where the early starts are worth it

text: Wildlife is the exception to the lie-in. Animals move in the cool of the morning, so a game drive means leaving before six. Udawalawe is the easy one with younger children: plenty of elephants, open country, and a shorter drive from the south coast than Yala.

body.alt: An elephant at close range on an early drive
body.caption: Udawalawe, just after seven. By ten, most of the animals are in the shade.

text: Sigiriya is the other. The climb is steep in places but short, and done by eight it is a highlight rather than an ordeal. After that, the afternoon belongs to the pool.

body.text: Mornings for doing things. Afternoons for the pool. It is the rhythm that keeps everyone happy.

text: Not every Sri Lankan beach is a swimming beach. Some have strong currents all year. We choose coast stays with a sheltered bay or a good pool, and match the coast to the season.

items: Every journey has its own vehicle and driver. Child seats are included, so tell us ages when you enquire and they are fitted before pick-up.
Pack light layers for the hills, where evenings are cool, and a hat for everyone.
Most hotels will do plain food for children without fuss. Rice, dhal and fresh fruit are everywhere.
Keep a swimsuit in the day bag. There is usually a pool or a river somewhere.

cta.heading: Tell us their ages, we will plan the pace.
cta.body: A travel designer comes back with a route built around short drives, good pools and the mornings worth getting up for.
